qa.answer: Four options. Move stage 2 to Takamori so Brightwater can prioritise stage 1 (USD 23K, no redelivery slip, recommended), ask Brightwater to resequence without a second source (USD 6K but likely refused), split all NGV volume to Takamori (USD 232K and a 22 day slip because of its 70 day lead time), or accept the dates and agree a 7 day move with Halcyra Airways (USD 63K in LDs).

Resequencing Brightwater's queue without a second source is cheapest at about USD 6K of air freight. It depends on Brightwater moving our stage 1 castings ahead of its date-of-order rule with no melt released, which it has little reason to do. The cheapest option that frees real melt and holds the redelivery is the recommended Takamori move at USD 23K.

In 2024 a US mill cut nickel superalloy allocation by 35% and Brightwater re-sequenced orders by contract priority (PRE-05). We split 60/40 to Takamori Precision Castings at an 8% premium for USD 118K, and engine inductions held. The lesson was to lock second-source casting slots in the same week the notice lands, because slots sell out within 10 days.

WO-2603 needs 24 stage 1 NGV castings at induction on 10 Nov. Brightwater's melt cut moves PO 4500018304-00010 to 1 Dec, 21 days late against 14 days of work-order float, so the Halcyra Airways redelivery moves 7 days to 21 Jan. The other six Brightwater lines slip 15 to 36 days but have no work order pegged, so no other redelivery moves today.
